output.title: When the metric stops matching the work
output.body:
When a metric stops matching the work, the fix is usually not to argue with the dashboard. It is to stop using that number as the primary signal and replace it with something that tracks the actual workflow step.

A common example is a repeating process where volume still looks fine, but quality or timing has drifted. The old definition keeps counting the wrong thing because the workflow changed, the rule changed, or the customer behaviour changed. At that point, the metric is no longer telling you what decision it was supposed to support.

For an owner, the practical choice is simple: either rewrite the metric, rewrite the rule, or keep a manual override for edge cases. Do not automate around a definition that no longer fits the work. That just gives you a neat number and a messy process.

The next step is to pick one recurring process and write down three things: what should be counted, who counts it, and at what point in the flow it should be counted. If you can do that on one page, you will see whether the problem is the metric itself or the workflow behind it. Once that is clear, the rest is a reporting fix, a workflow redesign, or a bounded automation question.
